rationale: While congenital hypotonia and muscle weakness are cardinal features highlighted in the initial identification of FILIP1-related neuromuscular disorder (OMIM #620775) and appear across multiple cohorts (e.g., Roos et al., 2023), subsequent reports demonstrate that generalized muscle weakness is not universal. Specifically, Watts et al. (2024) documented an affected individual with bi-allelic FILIP1 involvement presenting in the absence of muscle weakness or typical congenital myopathy features. In addition, large-scale cohorts such as Schnabel et al. (2023) characterized the presentation predominantly as arthrogryposis multiplex congenita with facial hypotonia, joint contractures, and microcephaly, without neonatal respiratory distress or severe generalized muscle weakness meeting a >90% frequency threshold across all described cases.

evidence.text: Five patients from four unrelated consanguineous families with homozygous FILIP1 variants presented with neurological symptoms including brain malformations, neurodevelopmental delay, muscle weakness, hypotonia, and dysmorphic features.

source.title: Bi-allelic variants of FILIP1 cause congenital myopathy, dysmorphism and neurological defects

conflicts: Watts et al. (2024) specifically documented the absence of muscle weakness and classic congenital myopathy in a patient harboring pathogenic FILIP1 variants, directly contradicting the premise that generalized muscle weakness is present in >90% of all affected patients.

While hypotonia is consistently reported across cohorts, it frequently manifests as facial hypotonia alongside arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, and neonatal respiratory distress is neither uniformly reported nor demonstrated to occur in >90% of cases.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true prevalence of neonatal respiratory distress and feeding difficulties across all molecularly confirmed FILIP1 cases worldwide?
new_directions.rationale: Published cohorts frequently highlight arthrogryposis and contractures, but detailed neonatal history regarding respiratory support and tube feeding is inconsistently quantified.

new_directions.question_text: Do missense variants with dominant-negative or altered protein stability (e.g., p.Pro1133Leu) produce more pronounced generalized muscle myopathy compared to complete loss-of-function/truncating alleles presenting as arthrogryposis multiplex congenita?
new_directions.rationale: Roos et al. (2023) identified distinct myopathic features in missense cases, whereas Schnabel et al. (2023) highlighted arthrogryposis in truncating variants, suggesting possible genotype-phenotype divergence.
